title: Spatial-Temporal Direct-Digital Beamforming Power Amplifier with Enhanced Back-Off Efficiency in a 24GHz Phased Array
problem: mm-Wave transmitters face degraded back-off efficiency when transmitting high-order constellations (PAPR 7-9.5dB for 5G+) while requiring efficient beamforming. Traditional architectures address beamforming and power back-off (PBO) separately—baseband beamforming increases complexity; RF beamforming suffers mismatch and insertion loss.
motivation: 5G and beyond systems require efficient transmission of high-PAPR modulated waveforms across phased arrays, but conventional separate beamforming and PBO approaches waste power and introduce complexity.
method: The Spatial-Temporal Beamforming Power Amplifier (ST-BPA) integrates direct-digital amplitude-and-phase beamforming with power back-off operation in a unified mm-wave PA architecture. This combined approach can be augmented with efficiency-enhancement techniques (Doherty, envelope tracking, or outphasing) to further improve back-off performance across the phased array.
key_novelty: Direct-digital spatial-temporal beamforming PA unifying amplitude/phase control and power back-off without separate baseband or RF stages.
contributions: Integrated beamforming and power-back-off reducing system complexity vs. separate stages
Direct-digital control over amplitude and phase beamforming in PA domain
Enhanced back-off efficiency for high-PAPR modulated signals (PAPR 7-9.5dB)
Compatibility with Doherty/envelope-tracking/outphasing for further efficiency gains
limitations: Not discussed; measured efficiency gains, scalability to larger arrays, and thermal management not characterized.
primary_theme: Integrated spatial-temporal PA beamforming for efficiency
